analysis: Batch 1.2 - law 501. The construction of Theorem 14 (proofs/paper/C05.md) gives a model for every n = 0, 1 (mod 4) up to 100 (50 of 50 tables satisfy the law); the sign identity prod_y sign(L_y) = (-1)^(n(n-1)/2) holds on all 39 semi-symmetric quasigroups of orders 3-9 that the SAT search enumerated; the case split finds a model of order 12 in its first case (idempotent, not a quasigroup); every certified order of 501 (gaps 2, 3, 6, 7, 10; members 4, 5, 9) agrees with n = 0, 1 (mod 4). H-C05-M confirmed. The model of order 12 was first seen in an exploratory probe of the open orders 11-13.
assumptions: the written proof of Theorem 14 (proofs/paper/C05.md) for all n; this experiment checks n <= 100
semi-symmetric quasigroups sampled: the first 6 models found by CaDiCaL for each n = 3..9, blocking each one found
falsification: A table of the construction failing the law, a certified gap at an order = 0, 1 (mod 4), or a semi-symmetric quasigroup violating the sign identity.

question: Is the spectrum of ETP law 501 exactly {n : n = 0, 1 (mod 4)}, as the parity argument and the group construction of Theorem 14 (proofs/paper/C05.md) say?
